text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- ICMS TAX EXEMPTION TO RAISE SOYBEAN AND CHICKEN PRICES

The proposed abolition of the ICMS tax on exports of primary and semifinished products, expected to be approved by Congress, is likely to raise costs for companies processing soybeans and chicken meat.
Public rates accounted for half of Brazil's 8.76 percent inflation rate so far this year. Discounting an increase in public rates, inflation between January and August would be around 4.8 percent.
-- SLIGHT DEFICIT IN BRAZIL'S TRADE BALANCE

Brazil exported $4.381 billion in August, a drop of 1.75 percent when compared with July. Import figures are still being calculated but Finance Ministry sources estimate imports should be between $4.6 billion and $4.7 billion. That means a trade deficit of nearly $300 million in August.

-- INFLATION SLOWS TO 0.34 PCT IN SAO PAULO
An increase in public rates and rental costs prevented Brazil from showing deflation in August, according to the Fipe Institute.
In September, inflation may be lower than March's 0.23 percent rate.
-- FGTS CREDITS TO BE USED IN PRIVATIZATION PROGRAM

Workers will be allowed to use funds from the Time Served Guarantee Fund (FGTS) to take part in Brazil's privatization program. The government plans to pay off a six billion real debt with the FGTS fund in bonds which will be accepted in privatization auctions, said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
